newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Palestinians protest at detentions in PLO jails.
newsitem.headline: Palestinians protest at detentions in PLO jails.

text.p: Members of six Palestinian opposition groups demonstrated on Sunday in front of the Palestinian Legislative Council in Gaza demanding the release of prisoners from PLO jails.

About 200 women and several men staged a sit-in organised by the militant Islamic Resistance Movement Hamas and Islamic Jihad, as well as radical PLO groups including the Popular Front for the Liberation of Palestine and the Democratic Front for the Liberation of Palestine.
Witnesses said PLO police arrested four demonstrators during the protests.
"We were hoping that our prisons would be turned into museums but we never expected to see the increase in the number of prisons," Hamas leader Abdel-Aziz al-Rantissi told demonstrators.
"We will continue our protest until all prisoners are released," he said.

The Palestinian Authority jailed scores of Hamas and Islamic Jihad activists, opposed to the PLO-Israeli peace deals, following suicide attacks carried out by Moslem militants in Israel killing scores of people.

Tensions between Hamas and the Palestinian Authority continued despite attempts by the Authority to hold reconciliation talks with opposition groups. Hamas, which attended one reconciliation meeting, said it would boycott further meetings until all of its prisoners were released.
A statement issued by the six opposition groups demanded the immediate release of detainees to pave the way for a national dialogue.
